newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan commander prays as Taleban jets bomb town.
newsitem.headline: Afghan commander prays as Taleban jets bomb town.

text.p: As the mosque in the mountain Afghan town of Jabal Os-Siraj filled up for Friday prayers, a Taleban warplane roared overhead prompting an angry response from an anti-aircraft battery nearby.
Some boys in the street outside the mosque ran for cover. "Bomb! Bomb!" exclaimed one of them with a nervous giggle.
A bomb crashed somewhere on the mountainside. There were no reported casualties in what was the Taleban's third sortie of the day over the town, 70 km (44 miles) north of Kabul.
Inside the mosque, none of the men at prayer stirred during the raid. The mosque's red threadbare carpet, whitewashed walls and green window frames were cool relief after the dusty bazaar outside.
Among the faithful stood Ahmad Shah Masood, the commander of forces belonging to the ousted Afghan government which is trying to dislodge the Islamic Taleban militia from the capital Kabul.
Masood's forces abandoned Kabul at the end of last month, giving the Taleban control of more than two-thirds of the wartorn country of 17 million.

Old men wearing tweed sports jackets over their long shirts and leggings, or "shawal kameez", knelt on blankets next to young fighters with ammunition clips strapped to their belts, all listening to a white-turbaned mullah.
"Jets from the Taleban are hitting women and children, people without sin," said the mullah angrily.
After prayers, Masood, 44, strolled outside towards a four- wheel drive vehicle with his modest armed entourage.

One of them placed an embroidered woollen blanket over his shoulders, his leonine features worthy of his nickname, "lion of the Panjsher", the treacherous mountain valley where he made his name as a mujahideen commander waging war with Soviet troops in the 1980s.
"You know where the frontline is and they (Taleban) could bomb there but as you can see they are bombing villages, they are showing their hatred of the Afghan people," said Masood.
"Only people who are not from Afghanistan could do this," he said, in a clear reference to Pakistan, widely seen as the Taleban's main backer.

At the funeral of 11 people killed in a Taleban air attack on the village of Kalakan, 25 km (15 miles) north of Kabul, on Thursday, one man said of the fundamentalist Taleban: "The Taleban are not Moslems, they are blasphemers, pagans."
Reuters cameraman Des Wright saw mourners run for cover as a Taleban jet flew over to make yet another strike on the village.
